scope: Post-H0.0 canonical planning handoff synchronized to current project registry generation 71. Preserve verified H0.0 as history and prepare a fresh-current-main H0.1 execution branch only after checkpoint integration; this Work Order does not create or execute C22 runtime.
required_outputs: Fresh post-checkpoint H0.1 execution epoch/control branch
Director-dispatched bounded C22 child Work Order
stop_conditions: Any runtime/domain change is attempted under this planning Work Order
C22 branch creation is attempted before a fresh post-checkpoint H0.1 execution epoch and Director dispatch
PC0 has an unresolved blocking RED
risk_reasons: H0.1 is the first controlled runtime-development pilot.
Incorrect handoff could authorize runtime from stale main or bypass H0.0 evidence.
Exact registry and main identity are checkpoint-critical.

design_brief.problem_statement: The H0.0 checkpoint must integrate without overwriting a newer main-owned registry generation 71 that carries fresh ECO research status, while preserving H0.0 R3 immutable evidence and keeping C22 runtime closed.
design_brief.current_behavior: H0.0 is terminal CHECKPOINT_PROPOSED and G8 is fully accepted/frozen. Current main advanced to 9ab5b163 with registry generation 71 for ECO P1/PH0/PH1 research status after the original checkpoint candidate was validated.
design_brief.desired_behavior: The checkpoint candidate preserves the exact current-main registry generation 71, Status/Plan/Resume select an H0.1 planning handoff pinned to current main 9ab5b163, and runtime workers remain zero. After merge, the pre-merge pointer is stale by design and cannot authorize runtime; a fresh post-checkpoint H0.1 execution branch must be created from exact new main. A separate post-merge registry generation 72 sync records the H0/G milestone in machine registry without losing ECO facts.
alternatives_considered: Overwrite the newer main registry with the older checkpoint snapshot
Allow the pre-merge planning pointer to execute runtime
Preserve current registry 71, repin R5 to current main, and defer milestone registry synchronization to a post-merge generation 72 control sync
design_brief.selected_design: Keep candidate registry byte-equivalent to current main generation 71, repin H0.1-R5 base identity to current main 9ab5b163, keep state PLANNED and runtime workers zero, then perform a post-merge generation 72 registry/frontier sync before any runtime dispatch.
design_brief.why_selected: It preserves the newer ECO machine truth, avoids a registry conflict, keeps H0.0 evidence immutable, and maintains fail-closed runtime authorization.
non_goals: No mutation of H0.0 R3 evidence
expected_risks: Main moves again before human merge gate
Runtime branch is created from pre-merge pointer
validation_plan: Validate current registry, H0.1-R5 epoch/work-order/event and output contracts
Require Plan=H0.1 PLANNING_ONLY with zero runtime workers and FORBIDDEN_UNTIL_DISPATCH
Run Status/Plan/Resume on exact candidate checkout or equivalent exact-head validation
Re-read main and PR head immediately before human merge

notes: Planning handoff only. Runtime remains closed. The actual H0.1 execution epoch is created from exact post-checkpoint main after this control-only checkpoint is integrated. Machine registry milestone synchronization is deferred to post-merge generation 72 so current ECO registry facts are preserved.
